title: Color and tint
nodes: TextureCoordinate → Texture Sample UVs. Texture Sample RGB × Vector Parameter Tint → Emissive Color. Surface / Opaque / Unlit. Tint (1,1,1) preserves the source RGB.
task: First set Tint to white: the untinted texture. Then reduce the red channel. Which source colors change, and why?

title: UVs and masks
nodes: TextureCoordinate R → subtract 0.25 → multiply 2 → Saturate (t). Compute t*t*(3-2*t) → Lerp Alpha. ShadowColor → A; Tint → B; result → Emissive Color. This is smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, UV.x).
task: Edit the 0.25 and 0.75 transition limits in the GLSL source, then Apply edit. These limits are constants, not MI sliders. Why does a color mask leave the plane opaque?

title: Texture and motion
nodes: TexCoord × Tiling → Add time offset → Texture Sample UVs. Use R → Lerp Alpha. In a Custom node use a TextureObject named BrushTexture; UE supplies BrushTextureSampler.
task: Set Speed to zero. Then double Tiling. Does the mesh move?

title: Light response and bands
nodes: PixelNormalWS and L → Normalize → DotProduct → Saturate → Step (X = light, Y = Threshold) → Lerp Alpha. Unlit output uses a direction parameter, not scene lights.
task: Raise Threshold. Which region grows? Keep N and L in the same coordinate space.

title: View mask and dark edge
nodes: PixelNormalWS · CameraVectorWS → Saturate → OneMinus → Power → Multiply EdgeStrength → Lerp Alpha. UE Fresnel with BaseReflectFraction 0 is a related native shortcut.
task: Try a pale edge, then dark purple. Why can a Lerp darken the edge while adding a positive color cannot?

title: Palette and brush texture (optional)
nodes: Brush sample R × 2 − 1 → Multiply influence → Add to light response → Saturate. Two Step nodes select three colors through two Lerps. The full UE playground adds a fourth color and editable thresholds.
task: Set TextureInfluence to zero, then .18. Change the palette without changing the band boundaries.
